title: Digestion Journey
text: Build a digestive system, then follow a sandwich from mouth to bloodstream. Students see what each organ does along the way.

quiz.question: In which organ are most digested nutrients absorbed into the blood?
quiz.explanation: The small intestine is lined with villi, which give a huge surface area for absorption.

title: Density Lab
text: Weigh an object, drop it into a measuring cylinder, read the rise in water level, then work out its density. A hands-on way to practise ρ = m ÷ V and reading a meniscus.

quiz.question: A stone has a mass of 60 g. It raises the water in a cylinder from 20 mL to 44 mL. What is its density?

title: Enzyme Factory
text: Explore how bacteria and enzymes help break down food, with a short mission for each enzyme.

quiz.question: Which of these breaks down starch into sugars?
quiz.explanation: Amylase breaks down starch. Bile is not an enzyme: it emulsifies fats.

title: Heart Hero
text: A mission-based journey through the circulatory system, made for World Heart Day.

quiz.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
quiz.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins bring it back.

title: Periscope Mission
text: Learn the law of reflection, then use it to build a working periscope.

quiz.question: In a simple periscope, at what angle are the two mirrors set to the tube?
quiz.explanation: At 45° each mirror turns the light through 90°, so it travels down the tube and out to your eye.

title: Rear Guard
text: Your phone camera watches behind you and speaks warnings in your earphones. It estimates distance with the pinhole camera model: the further away something is, the smaller its image.

quiz.question: A person's image on the camera screen becomes half as tall. If they haven't changed, how far away are they now?
quiz.explanation: Image height is inversely proportional to distance, so half the image height means twice the distance.
